system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The alert should not go out as written. The only verified input is a no-notice internal drill message, but the alert presents a live, observed ballistic missile threat to the public: status Actual, certainty Observed, severity Extreme, and the words "THIS IS NOT A DRILL". No input reports a real missile, so no hazard fact supports any public alert. Whether to send anything, and how to stop or correct this one, is for a person to decide.

objections.issue: The status is Actual, but the only verified input is an internal drill message. Actual means the alert is actionable by the whole public. A drill message may only be actionable by the designated exercise participants.
objections.fix: Do not issue a public Actual alert. If anything is sent, use status Exercise, limit it to the drill participants, and put an exercise identifier in the note. A person must decide whether any message is sent at all.

evidence.quote: No-notice internal drill message played by phone to the State Warning Point
Actionable only by designated exercise participants

objections.issue: The certainty is Observed and the severity is Extreme, which assert that a missile threat has been determined to be happening. No input reports an actual missile. The input describes only a drill script copied from the checklist meant for a real attack.
objections.fix: Do not assert an Observed or Extreme missile threat. No real hazard is reported in the inputs.

The ballistic missile checklist was intended for use in connection with a real ballistic missile attack.

objections.issue: The description says the event is not a drill and leaves out the 'Exercise, Exercise, Exercise' framing that came before and after the source message. This reverses the meaning of the input.
objections.fix: Remove "THIS IS NOT A DRILL". Any drill traffic must clearly say it is an exercise.
